python.definition: High-level, interpreted programming language widely used for machine learning, data analysis, web backend APIs, and automation.

sql.definition: Standard domain-specific language for storing, querying, manipulating, and retrieving relational data across enterprise databases.

machine learning.definition: Branch of artificial intelligence focusing on algorithms that learn patterns from training data to make predictions or decisions without explicit programming.

react.definition: Declarative, component-based JavaScript library developed by Meta for building dynamic, reactive user interfaces and single page applications.

docker.definition: OS-level virtualization platform for packaging software applications and their exact dependencies into isolated, reproducible containers.

git.definition: Distributed version control system for tracking changes in source code during software development, enabling branching, merging, and collaboration.

power bi.definition: Microsoft business analytics service providing interactive visualizations and business intelligence capabilities with an interface for reports.

tableau.definition: Visual analytics platform transforming raw data into intuitive, interactive dashboards, visual charts, and exploratory business reports.

aws.definition: Amazon Web Services comprehensive cloud computing platform offering compute (EC2), storage (S3), databases (RDS), and serverless architectures.

kubernetes.definition: Open-source container orchestration platform for automating deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications.

data structures.definition: Specialized formats for organizing, processing, retrieving, and storing data efficiently in memory (arrays, linked lists, trees, graphs, hash tables).

algorithms.definition: Step-by-step procedures or formulas for solving problems and computational tasks with defined time and space complexities.
